episodes.173270: A cold front crossed central Pennsylvania during the late morning and afternoon of October 13, 2022, accompanied by a broken line of gusty rain showers. Although this activity was convective in nature, it was too low-topped to produce any lightning. One such shower produced wind gusts near 50 mph, knocking down a handful of trees near DuBois in Clearfield County and a couple of rotting trees near Brockport in in Elk County.
episodes.173281: Storms moved to the south and southwest across the waters and produced several marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.173282: An early morning lightning strike damaged a residential home.
episodes.173283: Two lines of strong thunderstorms pushed southeast across the region.  The first during the late afternoon and early evening hours, and the second during the mid to late evenign hours. Both lines resulted in isolated wind damage.
episodes.173342: Locally heavy rain fell in parts of southeastern Pennsylvania on the evening of October 13.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2 to 3 inches.
episodes.173361: Modest instability and ample shear residing along a warm front favored thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across local coastal waters.
episodes.173500: Storms developed along a cold front producing widespread wind gust reports. Peak reported wind gust was 87 mph.
episodes.173638: Pre-frontal strong storms moved southward across the local Atlantic waters during the early morning hours.
episodes.174048: A cold front moved through Arkansas and brought severe thunderstorms to the state.
episodes.174148: On the afternoon of October 12th, warm and moist air was in place ahead of a potent cold front. Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed in the open warm sector ahead of the front. In the presence of limited low level shear but adequate deep layer shear, some storms took on supercellular characteristics with large hail and damaging winds closer to the cold front and brought an additional round of strong, damaging winds into the overnight.
episodes.174208: A line of storms developed along a cold front that swept through Central New York. While winds were gusty, most gusts were below severe criteria. Some stronger gusts were observed in Broome County where power lines and a transformer were damaged.
episodes.174262: A longwave trough progressed east from the Plains into the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the day on October 12th, which reinforced a cold front southeast into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon. Above normal temperatures and humidity for mid-October was observed ahead of the front, which focused an area of moderate instability across Southern Arkansas and North Louisiana, as large scale forcing increased ahead of the approaching trough axis. This resulted in the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of North-Central Louisiana and Southern Arkansas during the late afternoon and evening hours, with multiple reports of large hail and isolated wind damage before diminishing with the frontal passage late that night.
episodes.174263: A longwave trough progressed east from the Plains into the Mid-Mississippi Valley during the day on October 12th, which reinforced a cold front southeast into East Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon. Above normal temperatures and humidity for mid-October was observed ahead of the front, which focused an area of moderate instability across Southern Arkansas and North Louisiana, as large scale forcing increased ahead of the approaching trough axis. This resulted in the development of scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of North-Central Louisiana and Southern Arkansas during the late afternoon and evening hours, with a 58 mph wind gust measured at the El Dorado Goodwin Field Airport during the late evening hours.
episodes.174704: An upper-level trough and attendant cold front rotated through the region during the afternoon and evening of October 12, 2022. The cold front interacted with a moist and unstable airmass to produce numerous thunderstorms across West Tennessee and north Mississippi. Several storms were severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.174862: Numerous showers and thunderstorms made their way across southern Florida as a cold front approached the region. Heavy rain fell with the passing storms leading to flooding across several metropolitan areas along the Atlantic coastline.
episodes.174974: An isolated thunderstorm produced wind gusts above 35 knots over the northern part of Corpus Christi Bay in the afternoon.
episodes.174976: Images and video were relayed through a broadcast media partner of a landspout type of tornado near Chapman Ranch.
episodes.175015: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with thunderstorms moving northeast in advance of a pre-frontal surface trough.  A significant upper shortwave trough was moving eastward over the eastern Gulf of Mexico.
episodes.175064: A short wave trough digging southward towards the Central Gulf Coast states provided ample lift for the development of convection. Moderate levels of mid level shear and instability aided in the intensity of the thunderstorms, producing several rounds of severe thunderstorms throughout the day.
episodes.175111: A strong cold front plowed across New York and triggered a narrow line of enhanced showers with little lightning. The line increased in strength over eastern Lake Ontario and continued across Jefferson and Lewis counties. A few notches were noted on the line on radar in a marginally favorable environment for weak tornadic spin-ups. While velocity values on radar were unimpressive for a tornado, and no tornado was observed, some wind damage did occur in Lewis County.
episodes.175313: A strong cold front pushed through central Georgia on the evening of October 12th, producing showers and embedded strong to isolated severe thunderstorms.

Law enforcement reports and pictures relayed from broadcast media indicated numerous areas of street flooding in Jupiter and Tequesta. Main areas include US 1 and Beach Road, Bridge Road and Old Dixie Hwy, Willow Rd and Tequesta Drive, Alt A1A and Eganfuskee Road, Cypress Dr. and Riverside Dr, and Old Dixie Hwy and Eyeball Avenue. A few cars were seen stalled in one of the pictures.||Law enforcement was required to close the following intersections: A1A and US-1, US-1 and Bridge Road, and A1A and Center Street. Rainfall observations from across the area were in the 5-7 inch range in just over 2 hours.
Trees and wires were reported down in Lowville.

A video on social media showed urban street flooding in the Brickell neighborhood of Miami. The water level appeared above the curb level and across the sidewalk. Radar indication estimated between four and six inches of rain fell in 3 to 5 hours across the area.
